items.why: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 and trade 1 ten. Tens: 5 + 8 + 1 = 14, write 4 and trade 1 hundred. Hundreds: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. That makes 643.

dropped the new thousand
forgot the trade from the tens into the hundreds
correct
items.why: Rough first: about 1,200 + 1,000 = 2,200. Then trade at the ones, tens and hundreds: 8 + 6 = 14, 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, 2 + 9 + 1 = 12, and 1 + 1 = 2 thousands. That is 2,224.

items.q: A shelf holds 425 boxes. Another 268 boxes arrive. How many boxes are there now?
misconceptions: took away instead of joining
correct
forgot the trade from the ones into the tens
slipped in the tens column
items.why: More boxes arrive, so join: 425 + 268. Ones: 5 + 8 = 13, trade 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 6 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 4 + 2 = 6. That makes 693.

misconceptions: took the small digit from the big one in every column
made one hop of ten too many
correct
traded across the zero twice
items.why: Count up the gap from 458 in friendly hops: 2 to 460, 40 to 500, 200 to 700 and 3 to 703. The hops add to 245.

items.q: How big is the gap from 289 to 500?
misconceptions: started counting up from the wrong number
lost a hop of ten
counted a hop of ten twice
correct
items.why: Hop from 289 to 300, a hop of 11, then from 300 to 500, a hop of 200. The gap is 11 + 200 = 211.

misconceptions: took the small digit from the big one in every column
forgot the trade in the ones
correct
forgot to take the traded hundred away
items.why: Count up from 278: a hop of 22 to 300, 300 to 600 and 34 to 634. The hops add to 22 + 300 + 34 = 356.

items.q: Leo had 240 cards, gave away 85, then bought 30 more. How many cards does Leo have now?
misconceptions: added both moves instead of taking one away
took away both moves
stopped after the first step
correct
items.why: Two moves, one at a time: 240 - 85 = 155 cards after giving some away, then 155 + 30 = 185 after buying more.

items.q: A bar shows a whole of 500. One part is 175. What is the other part?
misconceptions: added the part to the whole
counted the gap with hops too big
correct
counted the gap with hops too small
items.why: The whole is 500 and one part is 175, so the other part is the gap: 500 - 175 = 325. Check: 175 + 325 = 500.

items.q: Team A scored 412 points and Team B scored 268. How many more points did Team A score?
misconceptions: added instead of finding the difference
counted a hop of ten twice
lost a hop of ten
correct
items.why: "How many more" means find the gap between the scores. Count up from 268: 32 to 300, then 112 to 412. The gap is 32 + 112 = 144.
